Reproduced host-local with the same binary: -S 3832054505 and -S 2147483648 exit 90 with the usage line; -S 2147483647 and -S 1 run (rc=0). The old draw put 10022 of 20000 seeds above INT_MAX. The detector fix is in the tree: tests/suite/fsx.sh now draws 1..2^31-1 (20000 draws, none outside) and keeps a failing check's fsx log on the node with its path in the record instead of deleting it. Nothing in the run is evidence about MeshXFS either way: fsx never opened its file.

change.cause: scripts/rig_lane.sh released a lane's configuration locks only through each holder's 1 s poll of the lane's pid (tail --pid), so for up to a second after a lane ended a lane started on the same configuration was refused as if the ended lane still ran; the lane's EXIT trap now kills and waits for every holder (release_holds), so the locks are free before its exit is seen

proposals.argument:
FIXED AND VERIFIED. The defect: scripts/rig_lane.sh held each configuration a lane names with a holder process (`tail --pid=$$ -f /dev/null`, scripts/rig_lane.sh:77) that sees the lane's exit only at its next 1 s poll, so for up to a second after a lane ended its configuration lock (/tmp/mxfs_lane.<configuration>.lock, flock -n at :70-71) was still held, and a lane started in that second on the same configuration was refused (rc 3) as if the ended lane still ran.

The fix (one site): the lane records each holder's pid (HOLDERS, :57 and :78) and its EXIT trap release_holds (:58-66) kills and waits for every holder, so the locks are free before the lane's exit can be seen. LANE_HOLD_RELEASE=0 makes release_holds return at once (:59), leaving the release to the holder's poll alone, which is the behaviour before the fix; recording the pids changes nothing else.

Cause, instrumented: the reproducer tests/lane_config_lock_lap.sh starts lane A (holds 64/net/mesh/direct 4 s), lane B while A runs (must be refused) and lane C the moment A's process has exited, and prints 'EXPOSED-RELEASE: lane C was started N ms after lane A exited' (N under the holder's 1 s poll) on every lap.

change.cause: the bmbt write chokepoint at bio submit (pal/linux/xfs_buf.c, the mxfs_buf_xfsaild_skip_bmbt_write test in the submit path) judged read bios as well as writes, reading the owner from the buffer's in-memory image; for a buffer an eviction had cleared of XBF_DONE, whose memory still held a deleted file's extent-tree leaf whose owner number had become a directory this node holds NL, it skipped the READ of the reused block: mxfs_bmbt_skip_preserve_truth staled the buffer and xfs_buf_ioend verified the old image and set XBF_DONE, so the reader was handed the other tree's leaf; the chokepoint now judges writes only (mxfs_bmbt_chokepoint_covers) and every read is issued

proposals.argument:
FIXED AND VERIFIED.

The defect: on 2/net/mesh/direct test1 read 2 of 8 files its peer had just written and fsynced and got no data. Its buffer cache served extent-tree (bmbt) leaves still carrying the owner of a file from the previous lap, deleted and its blocks reused for the new files' trees; the btree owner check refused them (P975-BMBT-LOOKUP-BAD same_image=0 flags=0x60) and the reads failed.

The cause, proven: the bmbt write chokepoint in the bio submit path had no direction test. For a read of a block whose buffer had been evicted (XBF_DONE cleared) but still held the old leaf in memory, the owner it read from that memory had become a directory test1 holds NL, so the predicate said skip: mxfs_bmbt_skip_preserve_truth read the LUN, found it different (P77-SKIP-DIFFERS same=0) and staled the buffer, the chokepoint printed P61-CHOKEPOINT-SKIP-BMBT and completed the bio with xfs_buf_ioend and no I/O, which for an XBF_READ buffer verifies the old image and sets XBF_DONE. The lookup then got the old leaf with XBF_DONE|XBF_STALE (0x60), exactly as P975 printed. Instrumented before the fix: lane tests/evidence/lanes/g2_bmbt_openefi_diag_20261023T072311Z (MXFS_EXTRA_MODARGS=bmbt_skip_reads=1, the old behaviour, which printed the direction): every P975 followed a P61-CHOKEPOINT-READ of the same daddr ('skipped, the old image is served with no read'), and 3 of 12 open-EFI laps failed.

The fix (one site): mxfs_bmbt_chokepoint_covers (pal/linux/xfs_buf.c:8840-8874), called at the chokepoint (:9692-9693), returns true for a write and, for a read, the knob bmbt_skip_reads (default 0): a read is always issued. bmbt_skip_reads=1 makes the chokepoint skip a matched read exactly as before the fix, since covers() is the chokepoint's only added condition; the function also counts each matched read (bmbt_chokepoint_reads), the lap's exposure. The readahead hold dbg_bmbt_ra_hold_ms (default 0) is test instrumentation, set to 300 ms in both arms so the synchronous read meets the readahead's buffer every time.
